scope: 100 distinct scoped review passes across existing SQL controls, model write contracts, adversarial cases, judgment guidance and release integration. These are not 100 exhaustive rereads of every repository file.
saturation: After 100 distinct scoped passes, no reproduced actionable gap remains within the implemented source/type/SQL proof boundaries. Dynamic or unresolved APIs, specialized domain transitions and database execution plans remain judgment work; this is not a completeness claim for arbitrary SQL services.

admission.failure: Discarded serial upserts despite a declared compatible bulk API.
admission.owner: Typed store command contract; no existing Sarj or Ruff rule proves this relationship.
admission.gap: Existing canonical-method checks did not inspect batch callers.
admission.harm: Repeated client/database work and independently maintained conflict policy.
admission.validBoundary: Unknown, incompatible, dependent, result-consuming and per-row failure contracts remain valid.
admission.smallestFix: A syntax/provenance-aware advisory requiring an existing typed bulk method; no autofix.

admission.failure: A plain same-table field UPDATE duplicates fields already writable through a typed upsert.
admission.gap: No previous control related setter SQL assignments to the existing command and conflict key.
admission.harm: Duplicated persistence policy and drift in validation, timestamps and supported fields.
admission.validBoundary: Guards, increments, distinct results, unresolved SQL and immutable/privileged fields are excluded or retained.
admission.smallestFix: A PostgreSQL parser and AST advisory; explicitly preserve update-only and unset/null behavior.

admission.failure: A bare cursor loop repeats one literal parameterized write without row results.
admission.owner: Psycopg cursor batching API and store operation.
admission.gap: No existing control checks driver provenance, invariant SQL and discarded per-row writes together.
admission.harm: Repeated client calls where the driver already supplies batch execution.
admission.validBoundary: RETURNING, result consumption, dynamic SQL, execute options and per-row transaction/failure handling remain valid.
admission.smallestFix: A driver-proven warning recommending an existing store bulk API or bounded executemany; no autofix.

admission.failure: Singleton upsert maintains a separate path or delegates into a bulk method that loops back.
admission.harm: Write-policy drift, repeated singleton work and possible mutual-delegation recursion.
admission.validBoundary: Only compatible required command/result signatures qualify; documented access and concurrency differences remain valid.
admission.smallestFix: Extend the existing owner and its delegation proof, retaining warning severity.

upstream.reasonForCustomRules: The new findings require relationships between Python method contracts, bindings, driver provenance and parsed SQL. Generic syntax/performance rules do not establish those relationships.

environmentFindings.resolution: The updated main already replaces the median gate with the same-rule warm CPU growth check and a measured quadratic control. Preserve that upstream fix; this change does not modify IaC tests or runtime source.

probes.note: Includes authored public examples and additional synthetic boundary probes; counts are evidence, not a claim of independent semantic coverage.

performance.method: 50 tracked Python files selected by sorted sha256(relative path), first process plus three fresh-process warm repeats, alternating baseline/candidate order; OS caches were not flushed; canonical-upsert expansion is included in both groups
performance.interpretation: Warm CPU increased about 7.7%; peak RSS was effectively unchanged. Warm wall time increased about 26.9% while other validation was running, so no speed improvement or isolated wall-time comparison is claimed. This measurement preceded the final narrowing of the canonical-upsert cycle condition; it is not presented as an exact-final-tree benchmark.

corpora.limitations: No additional mature public checkout was available locally; no external repository was cloned or fetched for calibration. Zero new natural matches does not measure recall; synthetic positives verify the supported proof boundary.
corpora.revisionScope: The combined four-rule run used the pinned source inputs. After restricting SQL extraction to method bodies, the affected field-update rule was requalified over the same inputs. The subsequent main sync changes generated release artifacts and unrelated detector source; the final repository gate evaluates the integrated tree. The final canonical-upsert refinement only narrows write diagnostics when the singleton has a distinct lock contract; it cannot add new corpus matches. The unchanged read diagnostics were classified against the original rule.

passes.evidence: Checked the supplied review's store contract; no bulk API is invented when it is absent.
Reviewed conflict policy, transaction ownership, row factories, pagination and SQL architecture controls before adding rules.
SARJ421 covered reads and status writes but omitted compatible upsert/upsert_many contracts.
Ruff's syntax/performance rules cannot prove a source-declared compatible model bulk API; no upstream rule is duplicated.
Verified Psycopg cursor executemany and pipeline behavior against official driver documentation.
Verified ON CONFLICT duplicate-key cardinality and conditional RETURNING behavior against PostgreSQL documentation.
Routed source/configuration semantics to code-standards rather than Git-tree policy.
Reproduced duplicate same-table bound field UPDATEs already represented by an upsert command.
Separated plain assignments from increments, guarded transitions, tenant predicates and version checks.
Selected warning-first diagnostics and no autofix because batch/failure and insert-versus-update contracts require review.
Negative fixtures require an actual upsert_many declaration.
Reject mismatched scalar and collection item annotations.
Reject mismatched scalar and bulk result annotations.
Match synchronous and asynchronous method contracts and call forms.
Reject bulk methods requiring additional context instead of guessing argument values.
Recognize both direct loop items and constructed commands depending on the item.
Skip repeated fixed commands whose relationship to the loop is not proven.
Skip writes whose result is assigned or consumed within the loop.
Skip loop bodies with notifications or additional statements.
Preserve conditional upsert branches rather than inferring independent work.
Preserve try/except and per-row error handling.
Skip break/else and other unsupported control flow.
Exclude async for rather than materializing an unbounded stream.
Recognize the declared singleton input keyword.
Reject unknown positional/keyword expansions.
Do not treat a rebound variable's old annotation as current API availability.
Resolve a uniquely assigned constructor-injected store attribute.
Review unique self-attribute injection and reject rebound self receivers.
Resolve first-party aliases without importing application code; reject rebound or mutated source owners.
Exclude generated/vendor code and statically empty/single-item literal loops.
Require locally source-resolved writable command fields.
Do not flag a field absent from the upsert command or its EXCLUDED assignments.
Require the same table and explicit schema identity.
Preserve PostgreSQL quoted identifier case.
Do not collapse distinct quoted/unquoted column names.
Require direct placeholder assignments rather than arbitrary expressions.
Require the same source and target field in upsert assignments.
Preserve COALESCE and other partial-update contracts.
Exclude conflict WHERE predicates and partial conflict inference.
Preserve version predicates in UPDATE.
Preserve additional tenant/authorization predicates instead of discarding them.
Preserve IS DISTINCT FROM and changed-row return semantics.
Exclude read-modify-write arithmetic and increment operations.
Exclude normalization/function expressions rather than claiming equivalent writes.
Reject joins, CTEs and multiple executable statements. Definition-time SQL in defaults is not a method-body write.
An UPDATE without a key predicate cannot establish equivalence.
Exclude ANY predicates, OR predicates and unsupported key relationships.
Leave ON CONSTRAINT, expression keys and unresolved identity to explicit review.
Require matching setter and upsert result annotations.
Keep an explicit warning about missing rows, creation and unset/null behavior; never autofix into accidental insertion.
Require a typed, import-proven Psycopg cursor.
Exercise imported aliases and synchronous cursor calls.
Invalidate an earlier annotation when the cursor variable is rebound.
Exclude f-strings, row-dependent SQL and runtime fragments.
Recognize import-proven psycopg.sql.SQL literal wrappers.
Reject unrelated/local SQL wrappers and mutated driver namespaces.
Only literal INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE writes qualify; SELECT and comment text do not.
Do not transform per-row result-set contracts.
Skip loops that fetch rows or perform additional cursor operations.
Preserve transaction and exception blocks inside the loop.
Exclude async streams and document bounded parameter batches.
Do not infer equivalence for unsupported execute options such as prepare overrides.
Cover positional tuples and named placeholder mappings.
Require bound values to depend on the loop target.
Keep malformed input and generated/vendor boundaries quiet.
Add upsert/upsert_many to the existing singleton-to-bulk owner.
Diagnose separately maintained singleton implementations.
Accept an awaited one-element delegation to the canonical bulk method.
Accept supported result extraction after a bulk write.
Preserve input binding when the bulk parameter uses a different name.
Reject a delegation that forwards another command.
Do not treat an arbitrary/multiple-row call as a singleton wrapper.
Reject an unawaited async bulk call as proof of delegation.
Do not accept a dead conditional call as the canonical implementation.
Require a real batch primitive; detect bulk-to-singleton loops even when the singleton also delegates back.
Document omitted, explicit null and supplied values as separate states.
Keep immutable/server-owned/privileged fields out of general caller write commands.
Review parameter, payload, pool and lock budgets without prescribing a universal batch size.
Require an explicit deterministic reject/merge policy before set-based upsert.
Document key-based result association, empty batches, partial failure and atomicity.
Require the actual shared connection/transaction boundary for logical multi-write operations.
Use structured error classification and retry the complete transaction with bounded backoff.
Retain increments, compare-and-swap and guarded state transitions.
Use representative query plans, tenant filters, index selectivity and referencing-side foreign-key costs.
Review streaming, backpressure, deadlines, pool waits, RETURNING and no-op audit effects.
Exercise local exact-code waivers without suppressing unrelated rules.
Verify positive warning findings retain exit status zero.
Execute source-owned positive and negative public examples through native rule adapters.
Synchronize warning lifecycle, rule inventory, ledger, public catalog and formatted examples.
Update Python/root versions, bundle/compatibility pins, adoption metadata and lockfiles together.
All final focused write-rule tests must pass.
Ruff, BasedPyright and all shipped custom rules must accept the implementation.
Verify the pinned tracked Python/SQL source corpus and its exact content digest.
Evaluate the first private corpus in isolated bounded native processes.
Evaluate the second private corpus independently with verified pins.
Use positive seeds and classify every inspected candidate finding; retain deliberate false negatives.
Check duplicate locations and separate existing advisories from new write-rule findings.
Compare first-process and repeated warm baseline/candidate CPU, wall time and peak RSS.

The complete make verify gate exits zero with exact installed tools, all native and packaged test lanes, docs, type/lint/self-lint and repository checks. Runtime selection and both code/calibration ledgers are resolved without weakening the checks.

The final diff review reproduced and fixed a false warning for a distinct singleton lock contract while retaining cycle detection. All 192 focused cases pass. No further reproduced gap remains in the supported boundaries. Upstream syncs pass 88 rollout/calibration cases and 377 adoption cases, preserving byte-identical Python rule source/tests from the green full gate.
